jobs.title: AI Operations Lead, Toast IQ
jobs.description:
Toast creates technology to help restaurants and local businesses succeed in a digital world, helping business owners operate, increase sales, engage customers, and keep employees happy.

About the Role:

Toast IQ is our agentic platform for local business: a growing set of specialized AI agents and capabilities designed to take real work off an operator’s plate, from driving demand and managing labor to optimizing the back office. As we expand this portfolio across multiple lines of business, we need to ensure that what we build comes together as a coherent platform, reaches the market effectively, and produces meaningful customer and business impact.

The AI Operations Lead will help build and run the operating system that connects AI strategy to execution and market impact. You will help shape how our AI portfolio comes together, is launched, and adopted, building the operating engine that brings this experience to life, and turning customer, market, and technology signals into better product and commercial decisions.

This is a highly cross-functional, hands-on leadership role. You will work directly with the VP of Product for Toast IQ, partnering across product, design, engineering, marketing, sales, and support to bring the vision of Toast IQ to life. Success will require strong judgment, exceptional communication, and the ability to personally drive ambiguous work to completion.

A day in the life (Responsibilities)

- Create visibility across Toast’s broader AI efforts and run portfolio ops. Connect work happening across the agent portfolio and other AI initiatives. Share learnings, identify opportunities to reuse capabilities, and surface key decisions. Maintain visibility into ownership, sequencing, dependencies, key decisions, risks, progress, and enablement.

- Build Toast’s AI presence. Partner with product, design, engineering, and marketing to make Toast’s AI products, technical insights, customer outcomes, and talent more visible through launches, customer stories, product and engineering content, and social channels both internally and externally.

- Turn high-impact ideas into action . Identify opportunities to accelerate Toast’s AI strategy, develop a strong point of view on what we should do, and have the ownership to run at the best ideas, bringing the right people together and driving the work from concept to tangible outcome

- Help shape the AI portfolio strategy. Partner with product and business leaders to define target customers, priority use cases, positioning, packaging, sequencing, and launch plans across Toast’s AI portfolio.

- Build an AI-powered engine that gets smarter over time. Use AI to continuously synthesize customer insights, product performance, market shifts, and changes in the underlying technology, turning signals from across the business into actions that improve our products, priorities, and how we bring them to customers.

- Turn a fast-moving AI market into an advantage. Stay up on what’s happening in AI and help translate emerging patterns into implications for Toast’s strategy

What you'll need to thrive (Requirements)

- Fluent with AI products, including how they work and what patterns are leading within B2B and consumer markets.

- 5+ years of experience in product operations, business operations, go-to-market strategy, or product marketing, with experience working alongside product and engineering teams.

- Demonstrated ownership of complex or emerging products from development through launch, internal enablement, customer adoption, and ongoing market learning.

- Exceptional written and verbal communication, including the ability to turn complex information into a clear narrative for customers, go-to-market teams, and senior leaders.

- Track record of building repeatable, cross-functional operating models.

- Strong product and commercial judgment, with the ability to translate technical capabilities into clear customer value and compelling market narratives.

- Ability to move fluidly between strategy and execution, from shaping a portfolio narrative or launch plan to improving a demo, creating enablement, resolving a readiness gap, or synthesizing customer feedback.

- Strong analytical skills and experience defining the measures that indicate whether a launch is working.

- High judgment and comfort operating in ambiguity. You recognize what matters, make defensible decisions, surface the right questions, and personally drive work to completion

What will help you stand out (Nonessential Skills/Nice to Haves)

- Experience bringing AI/ML, agentic, platform, or other rapidly evolving technical products to market.

- Experience building a launch, commercialization, or adoption motion.

- Experience in a startup or high-growth environment where the role required significant range and adaptability.

- Experience developing customer proof, product demonstrations, or technical thought leadership.

- Vertical SaaS, SMB, or restaurant and hospitality technology experience.

- Familiarity with AI product evaluation and the commercial considerations associated with AI products.

- BA/BS or equivalent practical experience

AI at Toast

At Toast, one of our company values is that we're hungry to build and learn. We believe learning new AI tools empowers us to build for our customers faster, more independently, and with higher quality. We provide these tools across all disciplines, from Engineering and Product to Sales and Support, and are inspired by how our Toasters are already driving real value with them. The people who thrive here are those who embrace changes that let us build more for our customers; it’s a core part of our culture.

Our Total Rewards Philosophy

We strive to provide competitive compensation and benefits programs that help to attract, retain, and motivate the best and brightest people in our industry. Our total rewards package goes beyond great earnings potential and provides the means to a healthy lifestyle with the flexibility to meet Toasters’ changing needs. Learn more about our benefits at https://careers.toasttab.com/toast-benefits .
The base salary range for this role is listed below. The starting salary will be determined based on skills, experience, and geographic location. In addition to base salary, our total rewards components include cash compensation (overtime, bonus/commissions if eligible), equity, and benefits. jobs.title: Associate, Sales Compensation Strategy and Operations
jobs.description:
Toast creates technology to help restaurants and local businesses succeed in a digital world, helping business owners operate, increase sales, engage customers, and keep employees happy.

Toast is looking for an Associate to support how we run and scale compensation for our sales organization.

You'll work closely with the Sales Compensation Strategy & Operations Manager and partner with the Commissions and Territory teams from day one. You'll own opportunity credit adjustments, applying sales policy and rules of engagement to get crediting right, and you'll own quarterly MBO consolidation and reporting. Reps rely on getting paid accurately, so precision and judgment matter here.

This role also has a builder side. Much of sales compensation work is still manual and reactive. You'll help redesign it into scalable, proactive processes using AI tools and automation. As you grow, you'll take on more analytical work: attainment reporting, quota analysis, and the insights Sales leaders use to make compensation decisions.

About the GTM Strategy & Operations Team

We’re a small, collaborative team that sits at the intersection of data, sales strategy, and go-to-market systems. Our work shapes how Toast’s sales org is structured, how territories and quotas are set, and how reps are paid. We move fast, stay close to the business, and take pride in building things that actually get used.

A day in the life (Responsibilities)

Sales Compensation Operations

- Manage a high volume of opportunity credit adjustments, applying sales policy and rules of engagement (ROE) to get crediting right, and escalate exceptions with a clear recommendation

- Process recurring data loads throughout the month

- Lead quarterly MBO (management by objectives) consolidation and reporting for sales managers, from collecting inputs to delivering final results

- Be a trusted point of contact for sales leaders and reps on crediting questions, explaining decisions clearly and consistently

Process Scalability & AI Enablement

- Design, build, and test AI-assisted workflows and automations, such as data cleanup and recurring reports, that cut manual effort on your projects

- Help shift sales compensation from reactive to proactive by building automated checks and alerts that surface issues early

- Write and maintain SOPs and sales comp policy documentation so processes are consistent, auditable, and not dependent on any one person

- Spot repetitive work across the team and propose better ways to do it

Planning & Analysis

- Support monthly attainment reporting and leadership-facing decks

- Help scale and elevate compensation reporting by standardizing recurring reports, improving dashboards, and automating manual refreshes

- Support plan design and quota analysis, such as modeling scenarios and pulling data for Sales leadership recommendations

- Partner with the Territory team to support the rollout of territory-based quotas, including data preparation, validation, and rep-level quota reporting

What you'll need to thrive (Requirements)

- 0–2 years of experience in an analytical or operations role, such as sales ops, revenue ops, finance, payroll, business operations, or consulting

- Strong Excel/Google Sheets skills and comfort working with large datasets

- High attention to detail, with ownership of accuracy when deadlines are tight

- Curiosity about AI tools and a habit of looking for a better way to do repetitive work

- Clear written and verbal communication

- A bias toward action and comfort with a fast-moving, high-volume environment

- Experience with Salesforce (CRM) or similar systems or willing to learn quickly

What will help you stand out (Nonessential Skills/Nice to Haves):

- Experience with sales compensation software (e.g. Xactly, CaptivateIQ, Spiff, Varicent)

- Hands-on experience using AI tools to build workflows, automations, or reusable prompts

- SQL fluency or experience with Snowflake, Sigma, or similar BI tools

- Familiarity with sales compensation concepts like quotas, accelerators, crediting rules, and pay mix

jobs.title: EMEA People Operations Lead (Fixed-Term Contract)
jobs.description:
Please note this is a 12-month fixed term contract.

Toast is driven by building the all-in-one restaurant platform that helps restaurants operate their business, increase sales, engage guests, and keep employees happy. Our PeopleHub team is the heartbeat of our People & Places function, responsible for building global scalable tools, systems, processes, and dashboards that support our employees at every stage of their employee journey. We are helping transform the way that the People and Places Team delivers service to employees.

As the EMEA People Operations Lead you will help build and deliver a frictionless employee experience across the employee lifecycle for our teams in EMEA and help shape a global "shared services" model as it scales. You will own front line support for employee inquiries including benefits and leave administration, alongside other operational activities and program delivery. This role carries real ownership: you are the person Toasters in EMEA come to in the moments that matter, and the person who spots what is not working and fixes it. To be successful you will bring a customer-centric and continuous improvement mindset, a proven ability to use technology and process to elevate the employee experience, strong stakeholder management, and experience in a shared services function within a global matrixed organization.

This role reports to the PeopleHub Manager and will work closely with the PeopleHub Director and across our global centers of excellence (COEs).

This is a hybrid role requiring 2 days a week in our Dublin office.

A day in the life (Responsibilities)

- Deliver front line People Services (Shared Services) support for the EMEA region across the employee lifecycle, including operations, benefits, leave administration, and compensation

- Serve as an escalation point for complex EMEA cases, resolving them accurately, compliantly, and with a high standard of service

- Track and report on metrics and service level agreements (SLAs) to measure service quality and provide insights for decision-making

- Spot what is not working and bring forward ideas to fix it, with the autonomy to test and implement improvements

- Drive continuous improvements focused on automation, standardization and scalability that improve the Toaster experience, increase efficiency, and ensure compliance with local laws and customs

- Build strong relationships with stakeholders across the People Team, Legal, Finance, and Business teams to influence change and drive adoption of an evolving service delivery model

- Be the local subject matter expert who can influence Global COEs on program design that is locally relevant and compliant while aligned to global principles

- Partner across the People & Places team globally to prioritize and deliver a variety of small to large, complex, integrated People team initiatives

What you'll need to thrive (Requirements)

- Professional fluency in English  and French (preferred), both written and spoken, with the ability to support Toasters and partner with stakeholders in both languages

- Typically requires a minimum of 8 years of related experience with a Bachelor's degree; or 6 years and a Master's degree; or a PhD with 3 years experience; or equivalent experience

- Significant hands-on experience within People Operations or Shared Services functions

- Experience operating in a matrixed structure, and influencing outcomes without direct authority

- Experience with new entity creation and creation of complete employee lifecycle processes

- Experience supporting Global HR Transformation: strategy, design, and transition of People Operations to create value for the organization

- Working knowledge of labour regulations, GDPR requirements and best practices to help ensure Toast remains compliant

- Familiarity with SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley), and experience working within SOX-compliant programs and processes

- Understanding of HR Technology, HR reporting, workflow, and auditing requirements (experience with Greenhouse, Workday, and ServiceNow is valuable)

- Excellent analytical, problem solving and decision making skills with strong attention to detail

jobs.title: Program Manager, Workplace Operations
jobs.description:
Toast creates technology to help restaurants and local businesses succeed in a digital world, helping business owners operate, increase sales, engage customers, and keep employees happy.

As the Program Manager, Facilities & Workplace Operations (AMER), you will serve as the strategic "Product Owner" for our Americas workplace environments and operations. In this high-impact individual contributor role, you will define, scale, and run our regional workplace experience program while laying the operational foundation for long-term growth. This position is equal parts operator, program manager, and cultural champion. You will oversee our outsourced partner vendor model, establish core SLAs and KPIs, design scalable Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), and deploy modern workplace technology—all while driving an engaging workplace culture aligned with our company values. We are actively building our operational infrastructure while running it in real-time. jobs.description:

The work is hands-on and close to the numbers, and it’s also where the strategic questions get answered: how each market performs, what drives unit economics, and where the business can operate more efficiently. - Use unit economics such as LTV/CAC to pinpoint what’s driving results and where there’s room to improve

jobs.title: Senior Privacy Program Manager
jobs.description:
Toast is driven by building the all-in-one restaurant platform that helps restaurants operate their business, increase sales, engage guests, and keep employees happy. We’re seeking an experienced Senior Privacy Program Manager to join Toast’s Legal & Compliance team who will play a pivotal role in shaping and maintaining a world-class privacy program. We are heavily leaned into AI automation efforts, and this is an exciting opportunity to help grow the program leveraging automation and LLMs.

As part of the dynamic and collaborative Privacy team, you will lead efforts to operationalize privacy requirements across our global operations. This is an opportunity to work on challenging and meaningful projects that make a difference in how we safeguard data and uphold privacy principles within the products and services we offer (both B2B and B2C).

Our Legal & Compliance teams are primarily concentrated in Boston, New York, Washington D.C., San Francisco, and Chicago. Candidates residing in these areas will be prioritized, as they will benefit from closer proximity to colleagues and greater access to company resources and events.

A day in the life (Responsibilities)

- Global Privacy Program Management: Develop and maintain Toast's global privacy program, ensuring compliance with laws and best practices across the US, Canada, Europe, the UK, and other countries where Toast operates.

- DPA Enablement: Help triage our Procurement queue and provide a first pass assessment of privacy risk and vendor stance against our standard DPA using pre-defined risk thresholds and protocols in conjunction with LLMs.

- Privacy Rights: Continue to mature our privacy rights process and program, including driving efforts to further automate how requests are processed alongside our vendor, Ethyca, and internal business teams and developing SOPs for use in responding to privacy rights requests.

- Privacy Reviews: Maintain our existing Jira queue for privacy review requests and oversee and improve on automation to generate a first pass privacy assessment that attorneys can  then refine/finalize. Work with business/product teams to implement mitigations identified during such privacy reviews.

- Operational Compliance & Risk Mitigation: Translate privacy requirements into actionable processes, develop and supplement privacy FAQs for different domains,  manage privacy risk registers, and conduct Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIAs) in collaboration with cross-functional teams.

- Training & Awareness & Data Governance: Develop and deliver privacy training programs, and collaborate on data governance frameworks for data classification and lifecycle management.

- Metrics & Reporting: Establish and track key performance indicators (KPIs) to measure program effectiveness and provide regular reports to leadership. Maintain and update the Privacy team’s Confluence page to serve as an internal resource to other teams.

What you'll need to thrive (Requirements)

- Typically requires a minimum of 12 years of related experience with a Bachelor’s degree or 8 years and a Master’s degree. Privacy certifications (CIPP/E, CIPP/US, CIPM, etc.) are preferred but not mandatory.

- 5+ years of relevant privacy experience. SaaS or tech industry experience preferred.

- Comprehensive knowledge of global privacy laws (GDPR, CCPA, PIPEDA, etc.), and the ability to apply them practically in a business setting.

- A willingness to roll up your sleeves and help the team achieve its objectives without being overly concerned about the precise scope of your role. We are an outcome oriented team that likes to lean in to get things across the line in a collaborative manner (while still having fun along the way!).

- Ability to collaborate with technical teams on data flows, architectures, and system design

- Strong project management skills, with the capacity to align privacy initiatives with business goals and manage multiple priorities.

- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to simplify complex concepts, and strong analytical and problem-solving skills with attention to detail.

- A working knowledge of AI tools such as Claude, Gemini etc. and a willingness to use AI solutions for privacy program management.

jobs.title: Senior Program Manager, R&D Talent Programs
jobs.description:
Location: Boston, MA - Hybrid position

Toast creates technology to help restaurants and local businesses succeed in a digital world, helping business owners operate, increase sales, engage customers, and keep employees happy.

As Senior Program Manager, R&D Talent Programs, you will own the Product/Design talent program end to end—strategy, structure, cohort experience, and stakeholder alignment—serving as the primary point of contact and the planner who builds the cohorts that become the next generation of Toast's Product and Design leadership. In this role, you will collaborate closely with the Early Careers team, who manages university partnerships and the talent pipeline, as well as the Recruitment team, who oversees candidate sourcing and requisition management.

Our Product internship program is where you'll start. As that program matures, you will design and build the talent programs that come next—extending to Design and the wider set of programs that develop talent across R&D. This is a role with room to define its own scope over time.

This role is ideal for someone who has built a talent program. You will set strategy alongside Product & Design leadership, then do the work that makes strategy real: securing headcount, establishing timelines, designing an evaluation bar, and creating an intern experience good enough that the best candidates say yes. You will work in close partnership with People Success Partners, Early Careers, Recruitment, Finance, Compensation, and Product/Design leadership.

This role sits within the R&D Operations team at Toast - we are on a mission to empower our teams to build great products efficiently, effectively, and at scale. We remove obstacles, foster alignment, and help teams focus on what matters most—solving real problems for our customers. We also play a central role in building the talent pipeline for the future.

A day in the life (Responsibilities)

- Own the Product and Design program  side of our internship and early-career programs —program design, structure, timeline, deliverables, communications, and intern experience once candidates are in the pipeline (sourcing, screening, and requisition-to-offer recruiting mechanics sit with Early Careers and Recruitment). Build a structure for managers to determine internship projects and team placements.

- Size and secure intern headcount each cycle, and partner with Early Careers/Recruitment to ensure hiring plans, timelines, and evaluation criteria set them up for success.

- Build world-class programming - including onboarding, an executive speaker series, intern showcase and capstone presentations, and cohort culture and community.

- Design the conversion process, including the evaluation frameworks, compensation packages, and “sell” experience.

- Keep stakeholders aligned and informed, from intern managers to leaders, on program direction, level, budget, and placement.

- Represent Product at university partner engagements and campus events set up by Early Careers. Partner with Recruitment to source market intelligence to keep our process and our offers competitive.

- Run end-of-cycle retrospectives and translate them into the following year's plan, growing this from a single-cohort program into a durable, multi-function leadership pipeline for Toast.

- Design and build new talent programs over time—identifying where R&D's biggest talent gaps are, making the case for a program to address them, and standing it up from a blank page.

- Embrace and advocate for the use of AI tools to accelerate product discovery, streamline execution, and explore new product experiences - helping shape how we build and what we build.

What you'll need to thrive (Requirements)

- 7+ years of relevant experience across talent programs, early career or university recruiting, program management, or R&D/Product Operations.

- A track record of building and growing a talent program—you have stood something up and scaled it.

- University, MBA, or early-career recruiting experience strongly preferred, including familiarity with campus recruiting calendars and competitive dynamics.

- Exceptional program management: you can hold many parallel workstreams, stakeholders, and hard external deadlines without dropping any of them.

- Proven ability to influence without authority—briefing executives, holding senior managers to commitments, and absorbing pushback while keeping the program on track.

- Sound judgment on talent, with the ability to build and steward an evaluation bar and calibrate fairly across dissimilar work.

- Outstanding written and verbal communication; you distill complexity into clarity for audiences from interns to the executive team.
